market_holds: Spot $16.515 at the 18:08 UTC seal, and Yahoo shows about $16.77 intraday on 11-23. The front-expiry straddle (Dec 18) implies 16.95%, which is about 10.5% event move net of ordinary volatility. The ATM spread is 76% of mid, so that figure is indicative only. Put/call OI is 0.12 (baseline). Two prior prints, both bmo and both up: +15.9% (2026-06-03) and +10.7% (2026-09-01). Each was a revenue beat with a guide raise. Run-in: 18.65 on 11-16 (+3.7% on the MiniMed Fit clearance) to 16.01 on 11-20 (-14.2%), then about +4.7% today. Over the same 11-16 to 11-20 span PODD fell 8.3%, XLV 5.7% and SPY 6.8%, and SPY bounced +4.9% today, so most of the run-in came with the tape and peers. Consensus (Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-16, Yahoo table of 9 analysts): Q2 FY27 revenue about $825-828M, which is +9.3% reported on the $757M Q2 FY26 base, and EPS $0.10. FY revenue consensus is $3.42-3.44B against a company target of about $3.43B. The FY organic guide is about 10.5%, including 1.0-1.5 pts from the extra week. The FY adj. EBITDA margin guide was cut on 2026-11-16 from about 16% to about 11.3%, solely for a $162M Blackstone minimum-payment charge; arithmetic from that implies roughly $3.45B of FY revenue. Barclays cut its target from $22 to $20 on 11-13. Mean target about $25 (aggregator, 11-15). The Earnings Whispers preview called sentiment 'clearly bearish'. Short interest unavailable.
view: The arithmetic says the Q2 revenue line is set almost exactly on management's own words. On the Q1 call the CFO said Q2 organic growth would be 'more comparable to the underlying' Q1 rate excluding the extra week, which was 'low double digits'. Low double digits, less about 1.5-2 pts of FX headwind, gives about $827-834M. Here the euro averaged about 2% weaker y/y over Aug-Oct and the yen about 6% weaker, against a business that is 72% international. That range sits on consensus. A beat needs organic above about 11%, and the easiest comp of the year helps: Q2 FY26 grew 7.1% organic, with a US order lull ahead of the Simplera Sync/Instinct launches, and this is the first full quarter of Flex + Instinct in the US. The guide looks conservative. Q1 underlying was about 11% and Q2 likely about 11-12%, so 10.5% for the year including the extra week implies roughly 7-8% underlying growth in the second half. The 2H comps (8.3% and 8.7% organic in Q3/Q4 FY26) are no harder than Q2's. That makes a third organic raise more likely than not, and consensus FY revenue sits at the guide rather than above it. Against that, three things. First, the euro has fallen about 5% since the Sept 1 guide (1.16-1.17 to 1.103), so any USD revenue figure and the EBITDA margin are under FX pressure; a hedging program has only just started. Second, international diabetes peers slowed hard in the Jul-Sep quarter: Dexcom international grew about 5% organic against 16% the quarter before, and Abbott's CEO flagged international CGM price competition and price cuts 'over the next few quarters'. MiniMed's international business, which carries Simplera, may be told the same story in its outlook. Third, the margin bridge from 9.9% in Q1 to a 2H-weighted target invites a sceptical read of any Q2 EBITDA shortfall. Net: a modest top-line beat and an organic raise are more likely than not, against a price that has de-rated about 12% since the last report, mostly on the tape. But the decisive lines (organic guide, international commentary, margin) are two-sided, and the FX and international-pricing headwinds are real. Lean up, not a recommendation.
unpriced: Possibly the 2H conservatism. Consensus FY revenue ($3.42-3.44B) sits at the guide, although the guide implies a 2H slowdown to about 7-8% underlying on comps no harder than Q2's. A third raise is therefore not in the published number. It is not clean, though. A newly public company that has raised twice is likely to be expected to raise again, and the FX move since September could offset a raise in USD terms.

recommendation.reason: The guide arithmetic leans up: Q2 has the easiest comp of the year, US Flex + Instinct is in its first full quarter, and the FY organic guide implies an unexplained 2H slowdown. The run-in is mostly tape and peers rather than company news. But consensus revenue already sits on the CFO's Q2 framing. The euro is about 5% weaker since the guide, and international CGM peers (Dexcom, Abbott) just reported slowing and price cuts. The deciding line is two-sided, so this does not clear 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: International organic growth in single digits, or management holding the FY organic guide (or trimming USD revenue for FX) while citing international CGM pricing. Either would make the 2H look like the guide rather than a sandbag.

self_critique: The up case rests on the guide being a sandbag, which is the most common and best-known pattern in a newly public company that has beaten and raised twice. Buy-side whispers likely already sit above the published $827.5M, and +10-16% reactions may have taught the market to expect a raise. On the other side, the down case is concrete and dated: peers' international slowdown, Abbott's explicit price cuts, and a euro 5% weaker since the guide, against a 72% international business with a margin bridge still to prove. That case is about as strong as the up case, which is why I hold near 56-57 rather than higher. In a tape where SPY moved 5-7% in days, a 13:00 ET bmo window is also heavily exposed to market noise.

P3's counterparty route (Dexcom, Abbott, Insulet) gave the only real counterweight. P7's guide-against-comps arithmetic gave the lean but not a 65 threshold. No step got in the way.
